paper_title: Searching for dark matter with a 1000 km baseline interferometer
suggested_experiment_name: Mainz-Krakow K-Rb-3He comagnetometer interferometer (Advanced GNOME / CASPEr-family)
coupling_convention: g_aNN in GeV^-1 as plotted on the y-axis of FIG. 4 (derivative/gradient coupling of ALP to neutron spins)
notes: Paper reports new 95% CL (CLs method) exclusion limits on ALP gradient couplings to neutrons (g_aNN < 1e-9 GeV^-1 at best), protons (g_aPP < 1e-7 GeV^-1), and electrons (g_aee < 1e-6 GeV^-1) from a two-station K-Rb-3He comagnetometer interferometer (Mainz-Krakow, part of Advanced GNOME / CASPEr family). Mass range 1e-22 to 4e-14 eV (frequencies 1e-8 to 11.6 Hz); below ~5e-20 eV limits come from the sidereal-frequency-bin analysis. Local DM density assumed 0.4 GeV/cm^3. No numerical table is provided; data_points are an approximate reconstruction of the neutron-coupling exclusion curve (Fig. 4) based on textual statements (best limit below 1e-9 GeV^-1, 1/f noise scaling below 0.1 Hz, peak field sensitivity ~1e-17 T, coherence-time degradation above 5e-2 Hz), hence moderate extraction confidence. Coupling type chosen as AxionNeutron per the headline neutron result; the paper equally constrains AxionProton (scale curve up ~2 orders) and AxionElectron (~3 orders).
